Implicit: docs/specs/pickup-coverage.md and docs/specs/INDEX.md. Addon: profile.py, workers/pickup.py, routers/pickup.py, evaluate.py, messages ja/en (only pickup.description) and tests under addons/intelligence/tests.

In listed files, some symbols are new or changed without being named in the list. evaluate.py: `_read_history` now groups segment rows and calls `watch_state`, and the new `_excluded_before` sits next to `_opened_before`. profile.py: new `WatchRow`, `WatchState`, `watch_rows`, `watch_state`, `playback_coverage`, `_version_4_engagement` and `signature_exclusions`, a `version_4` kwarg on `profile_history`, and the public `engagement` is removed. All of these implement named touch points: `_HISTORY_SQL`, the targets, `_rank_configs`, `engagement`, `watch_signature`, `watched_file_ids` and `profile_history`. A grep found no caller of the removed `engagement` outside these files.

routers/pickup.py now reads the core DB via `profile_mod.watched_file_ids` (get_litloft_db, opened with mode=ro at app/database.py:2384/2421). This is 'the serving filter' touch point, and it stays inside the read-only rule in design-decisions.

restrict.ts keeps its `watch` option (frontend/src/components/videoapp/restrict.ts:20) as the spec requires. Recommended no longer passes it in useDiscover.ts:351-358 or useProviderShelfPage.ts:230-237. Addon shelves never passed it.

I5 holds by construction. `_stale_work` (workers/pickup.py:279-282) and `watched_file_ids` (profile.py:614) both derive the set from `signature_exclusions(watch_signature(...))`, and the router calls `watched_file_ids`. PROFILE_VERSION is 5.

I4: routers/pickup.py:88-100 loads every stored id in rank order, removes the excluded ids, and slices the kept list by offset/limit, or for daily takes the first min(40, len(kept)) and shuffles them with the existing seed. total is len(kept).
potential_unspecified_behavior: Every feed read now loads the whole stored feed (up to 300 rows) and the viewer's full watch history joined with played_segments from the core DB. The spec accepts this cost (Non-functional), but the home Pickup row and Discover now pay it on each request.

The signature now stores the parsed `played_at` (str of a naive datetime) where it used to store the raw text. Two unparseable `last_played_at` values both map to "", so a change from one unparseable string to another no longer moves the checkpoint. I found no case where that changes the feed, because unparseable rows are excluded and never seed.
regression_risks: The removed public `profile.engagement` would break any out-of-tree caller. A grep of addons/intelligence found none.
The router now depends on the core DB being reachable. If that read fails, the whole feed request fails, which the spec's failure table accepts and test_z_pickup_coverage_endpoint pins.
The core frontend change must ship together with the submodule bump. If it shipped against an addon without the serving filter, watched videos would reach Recommended until the next sweep.
test_coverage: test_z_pickup_coverage_profile.py tests coverage arithmetic (the 99 s and 20 s edges, segments past the duration, other viewers, non-finite durations), the short-video rule, the legacy boundary at R including offset timestamps, and the state transitions.

test_z_pickup_coverage_endpoint.py tests filtering, paging, the daily window against an oracle feed that never held the removed ids, and per-viewer and per-drive isolation, and checks that a failed exclusion read fails the request.

test_z_pickup_coverage_worker.py tests that the three readers agree (I5), that a checkpoint moves exactly once for each signature field, and that the previous feed is kept when history cannot be read.
test_z_pickup_engagement.py is unchanged. It uses NOW 2026-06-15 (legacy), so it still pins version 4's engagement and exclusion under I3.
The core tests now assert `watch` is undefined on every Recommended restrict, both on Discover (including the rebuild from stored ids) and on the See all page.
